model: Orbital Economy v7.7.15 Wage Pricing candidate r1
note: Task 037: all seven annotations required by architecture specification section 5. Regional pairs are annotated on A and apply to B through applies_to_mirror. Merge parameters into the accepted annotations for the candidate registry; do not replace the accepted annotations.

Wage Pricing Enabled.role: Switch for proportional wage pass-through into ore, energy and food prices and price-responsive final demand; default 0, enabled only in Modes 54-55.
Wage Pricing Enabled.effect: At 0 every wage_pricing replacement keeps the accepted formula. At 1 regional prices are multiplied by Max(1 + labor_share * relative_wage_change, 1e-6), and effective metal/electronics demand by its price demand factor.
Wage Pricing Enabled.evidence: docs/tasks/037-wage-pricing/V7_7_15_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md sections 1, 3, 5; docs/research/FINANCE_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-12_RU.md: owner intermediate-step decision, proportional pass-through and price demand only.

Price Demand Elasticity.role: Positive price elasticity magnitude eta = 0.5, shared by regional metal and electronics final demand.
Price Demand Elasticity.effect: Price Demand Factor = Max(market_price / reference_price, 1e-6)^(-eta). It scales the previous Effective Local Base Demand, preserving the population and earlier layers; household income does not enter demand in this step.
Price Demand Elasticity.evidence: docs/tasks/037-wage-pricing/V7_7_15_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md sections 1, 5; docs/research/FINANCE_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-12_RU.md: owner selects price demand with eta 0.5; elasticity is an explicit prototype calibration, not an estimated law.

A Food Labor Share.role: Symmetric food-price labor shares A = 1, B = 1: initial unit labor cost divided by initial food price, capped at 1.
A Food Labor Share.effect: Scales proportional regional food-price response to wage / initial_wage - 1. Food labor intensity 0.15 times initial wage gives 15 in A and 21 in B, above the initial food-price index near 10, so both ratios are capped at 1. It avoids the additive prototype's food-price collapse when B wages fall.
A Food Labor Share.evidence: docs/tasks/037-wage-pricing/V7_7_15_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md sections 1, 5; docs/research/FINANCE_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-12_RU.md: first-year Mode 52 reference levels on v7.7.14, proportional form and conclusions 3-4 about labor costs exceeding food prices.

A Ore Labor Share.role: Asymmetric ore-price labor shares A = 1, B = 0.5: initial unit labor cost / initial ore price, capped at 1, using first-year Mode 52 levels on v7.7.14.
A Ore Labor Share.effect: Scales each region's proportional ore-price response to its relative wage change. The A ratio exceeds 1 and is capped; B retains the prototype ratio 0.5. Initial prices remain unchanged when the relative wage change is zero.
A Ore Labor Share.evidence: docs/tasks/037-wage-pricing/V7_7_15_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md sections 1, 5; docs/research/FINANCE_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-12_RU.md: proportional pass-through and conclusion 4 (ore A capped, ore B share 0.5).

A Energy Labor Share.role: Asymmetric energy-price labor shares A = 0.83, B = 1: initial unit labor cost / initial energy price, capped at 1, using first-year Mode 52 levels on v7.7.14.
A Energy Labor Share.effect: Scales proportional energy-price response to regional relative wage change. A retains the prototype ratio 0.83; the B ratio exceeds 1 and is capped at 1. The region's own wage drives its price, with the previous formula retained at switch 0.
A Energy Labor Share.evidence: docs/tasks/037-wage-pricing/V7_7_15_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md sections 1, 5; docs/research/FINANCE_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-12_RU.md: proportional pass-through and conclusion 4 (energy A share 0.83, energy B capped).

A Metal Demand Reference Price.role: Asymmetric reference metal prices A = 25.9, B = 34.46, the regional mean market prices over the first year of Mode 52 on accepted v7.7.14.
A Metal Demand Reference Price.effect: Denominator of the metal price ratio raised to -Price Demand Elasticity; normalises demand response to each region's baseline price level rather than imposing a common A/B price.
A Metal Demand Reference Price.evidence: docs/tasks/037-wage-pricing/V7_7_15_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md sections 1, 5; docs/research/FINANCE_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-12_RU.md: reference values are first-year Mode 52 means. Fixed owner calibration A 25.9 / B 34.46.

A Electronics Demand Reference Price.role: Asymmetric reference electronics prices A = 23.1, B = 21.91, the regional mean market prices over the first year of Mode 52 on accepted v7.7.14.
A Electronics Demand Reference Price.effect: Denominator of the electronics price ratio raised to -Price Demand Elasticity; preserves regional reference price levels when scaling effective electronics demand.
A Electronics Demand Reference Price.evidence: docs/tasks/037-wage-pricing/V7_7_15_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md sections 1, 5; docs/research/FINANCE_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-12_RU.md: reference values are first-year Mode 52 means. Fixed owner calibration A 23.1 / B 21.91.
